findings: Attack surface: no new dependency (standard library only: signal, threading added in tools/claude_station.py), no new endpoint, no new outbound call, no new permission. The CLI is still launched from an argument list without a shell (tools/claude_station.py run_with_ceiling uses subprocess.Popen(command) with a list); the only command change replaces the 'json' output format token with 'stream-json' and appends --verbose, both constants.

Input validation, fail closed: efficiency.station_budgets and default_station_budget are allow-list validated (non-empty string station ids, positive non-bool integers) and reject rather than repair (anvil/config.py station_budget_settings, _positive_tokens); an over-cap worst case raises naming the pipeline and excess. ANVIL_STATION_BUDGET_TOKENS / ANVIL_STATION_PARTITION are parsed as positive integers and a malformed value ends the wrapper with exit 10 before any model call (parse_ceiling). With require_usage set an unmeasured station is refused, never treated as zero (anvil/telemetry.py precall_decision).

Untrusted model/CLI output: streamed stdout lines are parsed with json.loads inside try/except, non-dict events are skipped, and usage is only read from dict-typed message.usage; it is used solely for arithmetic and the kill decision, never executed, never used as a path. Low severity residual: if the CLI stream carries no usage events (format change), the in-flight ceiling silently never trips, so the ceiling fails open to the outer max_run_tokens bound and the pre-call check. Recommend a follow-up that records 'ceiling unmeasured' when a ceiling was set but no usage was streamed.

Process lifecycle, low severity, not a blocker: run_with_ceiling starts the CLI with start_new_session=True and kills it with os.killpg(SIGKILL) on ceiling or timeout, which correctly reaps the CLI's own children. However if the wrapper itself is killed from outside (anvil/executor.py subprocess.run timeout kills only the wrapper PID), the CLI child now sits in its own session and survives, continuing to spend tokens with no supervisor. The non-ceiling path had the same orphaning before this change (subprocess.run kill is PID-only), and the wrapper's station timeout fires below the executor timeout, so exposure is limited. Recommend a follow-up: a SIGTERM handler in the wrapper that forwards to the child's process group.

Secrets and logging: no secret, token or key added to the tree (anvil.yaml change is the 14-entry partition table only, summing to 15000000). New stderr and reason strings carry station ids, token counts and partition sizes only; no environment value or header is echoed. Recorded budget_exceeded usage records carry the same honest fields as the timeout record.

Paths: completeness_gaps (anvil/runner.py) checks existence of the builder report path from configuration and of test-writer delta entries computed from the local working-tree snapshot, joined under the project root; these are internal values, not externally supplied, and are only stat'ed, not written. The gap strings flow back into the builder loopback packet as text; they contain repo-relative file names only, which is acceptable.

Copilot runtime: the in-flight ceiling is explicitly disabled with a stderr notice because Copilot exposes usage only at session end; the pre-call check and run cap still apply. This is a documented limitation, not a silent bypass.

Evidence: python -m unittest tests.test_station_budgets_completeness ran 26 tests, OK. Protected paths (pipelines/, anvil.json, existing tests) are untouched per git status. No em or en dash found in changed or new files.
